cards.text: Jacob's back on the road, heading home with his whole household. Friend, I know a little something about angels showing up when you least expect it. Because right there on the way, the angels of God meet him.

cards.question: Jacob sees the angels of God right there on the road. What does he say?

answers.text: This is the camp of God
This is the gate of heaven
This is the mountain of God

cards.text: So Jacob names that place Mahanaim. Then he sends messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau, in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.

cards.question: In the message Jacob sends to his brother Esau, how does Jacob describe himself?

answers.text: As the head of the family

cards.text: Jacob's message says he's been staying with Laban all this time. Then he lists what he's got now: oxen, donkeys, flocks, menservants and maidservants.

cards.question: Jacob tells Esau why he's sending this message. What reason does he give?

answers.text: So he may find favor in Esau's sight
So Esau will send him supplies
So Esau will come and live with him

cards.text: The messengers come back. I'd LOVE to tell you Esau just sent a nice note back, but no: Esau is coming to meet Jacob in person.

cards.question: Esau is on his way to meet Jacob. Who's coming with him?

cards.text: FOUR. HUNDRED. MEN. You ever get a text from your boss that just says "call me"? Now multiply that feeling by four hundred, because Jacob is in great fear and distress.

cards.question: Jacob is in great fear and distress. What does he do with his people and his animals?
Jacob's plan with the two camps: if Esau attacks one camp, the other camp can ___.

cards.text: Then Jacob prays. He calls on the God of his father Abraham, the God of his father Isaac, the LORD who told him to go back home and said, 'I will make you prosper.'

cards.question: In his prayer, Jacob tells God he deserves all the kindness and faithfulness God has shown him.

cards.text: Jacob crossed the Jordan with only his staff, and now he's become two camps. The man left with a STICK and came back needing a SECOND campground.

cards.question: In his prayer, what does Jacob ask God to do?

answers.text: Lead him safely back to Laban
Send the angels to fight for him

cards.question: Jacob tells God he's afraid Esau may come and attack him and the mothers and children with him.

cards.text: Then Jacob wraps up his prayer by reminding God of something God Himself said. I think Jacob's holding on to that promise with both hands.

cards.question: At the end of his prayer, Jacob reminds God of a promise God made him. What is it?

answers.text: Offspring like the sand of the sea
A land flowing with milk and honey
A throne that will last forever

cards.text: Jacob spends the night there. And from everything he brought with him, he picks something out for his brother Esau.

cards.question: Jacob picks something out for Esau from everything he brought with him. What is it?

cards.text: And this is no small gift: female goats, male goats, ewes, rams, milk camels with their young, cows, bulls and donkeys, hundreds of animals, starting with 200 female goats. When I give somebody a gift, it fits in a cookie box. Jacob's gift needs its own ROAD.
Jacob splits the animals into separate herds and hands each herd to his servants. Then he tells them to go on ahead of him.

cards.question: Jacob's servants are taking the herds on ahead. What does he tell them about the herds?

cards.text: Then Jacob gives the servant in the lead his lines. When Esau meets him and asks whose animals these are, here's what he's supposed to say.

cards.question: Esau asks the lead servant whose animals these are. What is the servant to answer?

answers.text: They belong to your servant Jacob
They belong to our master Laban
They belong to the king of Edom

cards.question: The lead servant is also supposed to tell Esau that Jacob is behind them.

cards.text: It's not just the lead servant: the second, the third and every servant after them gets the same speech for Esau. That's not a gift anymore, friend, that's a PARADE with a SCRIPT.

cards.question: Jacob thinks to himself: I will ___ Esau with the gift going before me, and after that I can ___ him.
Jacob is sure that once Esau gets the gifts, Esau will accept him.

cards.text: So Jacob's gifts go on ahead of him, and Jacob spends the night in the camp. And that's where we'll leave him for now, friend, but trust me, Jacob's story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Laban appears for the first time in this lesson, and the card doesn't say who he is (Jacob's uncle, whose daughters Jacob married, Gen 29).

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The summary card for the gift list (32:14-15) names every kind of animal one after another instead of summing up the stretch in a few words.

rule.text: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item.

findings.problem: The story card is three sentences long. It isn't the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The line saying the story isn't over nearly copies the doc's example ("And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.") instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin's line "I know a little something about angels showing up when you least expect it" calls back to the angel visiting him in the drawer. The joke logic test only confirms that bakers know about the junk drawer from onboarding. It doesn't say whether they know about the angel's visit.
findings.question: Does onboarding tell bakers about the angel calling Papa Dorin out of the drawer? If it does, can callbacks to the angel be used without setting it up in the lesson?
